problem: Lack of practical integration of non-networked (decentralized) sanitation systems into academic curricula for sustainable urban development in India
solution: SCBP (Sustainable City Building Programme) partners with universities to develop and implement modular educational content, workshops, and research projects focused on non-networked sanitation systems. This includes creating interdisciplinary curricula, hands-on activities, and state-level capacity-building initiatives.
technology: Participant Kit (modular educational toolkit for water and sanitation) designed for integration into architectural/engineering curricula, featuring four themed modules covering sanitation systems, policies, technologies, and community engagement
outcome: Successful implementation of 9 university partnerships, training over 500 students and professionals, and initiating state-level workshops (e.g., Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu) to pilot decentralized sanitation systems and build operational capacity for FSTPs (Fecal Sludge Treatment Plants)
